Section 3. Service terms excerpt attached to the invoice
The following provisions were attached to invoice GR-66108 and acknowledged by Harbor Labs when the booking was confirmed. They apply to refund requests and booking amendments for this event. The provisions are reproduced here because the date calculation depends on the exact triggering event and the stated counting convention.

Clause 4.1, Booking confirmation: A booking becomes confirmed when the vendor issues the final invoice and the customer’s payment has settled. An estimate, preview, purchase order, or payment instruction is not, by itself, a confirmed booking. If the invoice and payment settle on different dates, both conditions must be complete before the booking is confirmed. The confirmation date in the account history is therefore 25 August 2026 for this file, because that is when payment settled after the final invoice had been issued.

Clause 4.2, Refund request submission: A customer may submit a refund request within 30 calendar days after payment settles. The payment date is day zero. A request is timely if the vendor’s web-form system records receipt no later than 23:59 local time on the thirtieth calendar day after the settled payment date. Staff review, acknowledgement, or decision dates do not alter the original receipt date. A request begun but not submitted is not a submitted request. A later document that merely refers to a request does not substitute for a submission record.

Clause 4.3, Refund request contents: The customer must identify the booking reference and the amount or service for which a refund is sought. Supporting material may be added after submission if the request itself is identifiable. The requirement concerns the content of the submission, not the day on which a reviewer finishes examining it. A request can be timely even when a decision is pending; a late request does not become timely because the customer later supplies additional documents.

Clause 4.4, Requests concerning more than one charge: A form may identify multiple requested adjustments. Each requested charge is assessed under the same submission date unless the form separates them into submissions with their own receipt timestamps. A question about an item is not automatically a request to refund it. A request for information, an estimate, a revised layout, or an optional service is not a refund request unless the submitted form expressly asks for a refund or repayment. Staff should retain the exact selection and comments entered by the customer.

Clause 4.5, Amendments: A customer may request a booking amendment within 10 calendar days after payment settles. The payment date is day zero. The request must reach the designated amendment form by 23:59 local time on the tenth calendar day after payment. An amendment request may concern quantity, schedule, or room allocation. A request to amend is distinct from a request for a refund, even if the same web form is used for both. A note in an internal planning worksheet is not an amendment request unless transmitted through the designated form.

Clause 4.6, Amendment review: Granite Rentals will acknowledge receipt of an amendment request, normally within three business days. This acknowledgement target is an administrative service target and does not determine whether the request itself was submitted within the ten-calendar-day period. Acknowledgement after a deadline does not make a timely submission late. Conversely, an early acknowledgement does not make a submission timely if the system receipt date was after the submission deadline.

Clause 4.7, Non-business days: The submission periods in Clauses 4.2 and 4.5 are calendar-day periods and do not move to the next business day when their final date is a weekend or holiday. Business days apply only to the acknowledgement target in Clause 4.6. The system accepts web submissions every day. The vendor’s office may not staff the account queue on weekends, but receipt is determined by the timestamp stored by the web system, not by when an employee opens the queue.

Clause 4.8, Duplicate records: When a customer submits the same request more than once, the system keeps each receipt timestamp. Staff may associate duplicate records with one case, but association does not erase or replace the individual submission dates. The earliest identifiable submission is considered the submission date for that request if it contains the necessary booking reference and requested action. A later complete submission does not necessarily displace an earlier complete one. The audit record should show which form entry was used.

Clause 4.9, Event date: The event date is relevant to delivery and performance planning but does not serve as the starting point for the refund and amendment periods in Clauses 4.2 and 4.5. Staff must not measure those periods from the event date, invoice issue date, estimate date, or the date a reviewer reads the submission. The applicable start date for this booking is the settled payment date.

Clause 4.10, Records and corrections: If a customer notices an error in a form, the customer may send a correction. A correction that changes the requested action is treated as a new request for the changed action, while a correction that only clarifies an already identifiable request is retained with the original submission. The reviewer must determine whether the first submission already identified the booking and the requested action. The internal receipt log and the customer’s submitted answers control; the date typed into a comment field does not supersede the server timestamp.

Section 4. Web-form submission export
The web-form platform logged an entry for booking HL-2048 on 4 September 2026 at 16:41 local time. The automated receipt number was WF-0904-1641. The entry identified Harbor Labs as the customer, entered GR-66108 as the invoice reference, selected “Refund request,” and included the comment: “Please refund the reception tables that were not required after the guest plan was reduced. We paid for the eight-table line; request repayment for that charge.” The amount field contained $560.00. The form’s submitted status was recorded at 16:41, not merely saved as a draft. The reviewer queue received the entry immediately, but a staff member opened it on 8 September.

The submitted form also included an attachment labelled “reception layout final.pdf.” The attachment metadata shows it was uploaded at 16:38 on 4 September. It contained the event layout and a note that the reception tables remained on the original invoice. The customer’s refund request was stated in the form comment itself, so the attachment’s earlier upload time does not determine when the request was received. The receipt screen displayed the system timestamp, and the customer downloaded that receipt on the same afternoon. The form did not select “Amendment” or “General question.”

The system history also shows a form draft created on 3 September at 09:11. The draft had the booking reference filled in but did not contain a selected request type, an amount, or a submitted status. It was abandoned before transmission. A saved draft is preserved for troubleshooting but is not identified as the receipt record. The system generated an unrelated automatic reminder on 2 September asking the customer to review the event plan. That reminder was not sent by Harbor Labs and was not a request of any kind.

On 9 September, Farid Haddad sent a message to Granite Rentals’ account desk asking whether the refund request had been routed to the correct team. The message referred to the form receipt number and asked for confirmation of the review queue. It did not change the requested amount or add a new item. The message’s sent timestamp was 9 September 2026 at 10:05. Granite Rentals replied on 10 September that the request had been assigned to account review. The reply confirmed routing and did not decide the request.

The review clerk initially coded the case as “pending review” on 11 September. The clerk’s screen displayed both the form receipt date and the date the queue was opened. The clerk did not treat the 8 September opening date as the customer’s submission date. An internal note dated 12 September says, “Check payment-relative cut-off; do not use event date.” A second note dated 13 September repeats that the exact submission timestamp is available in WF-0904-1641. These notes are administrative reminders; the actual date remains the platform’s recorded receipt date.

An additional form entry appears in the export on 15 September at 12:02, receipt number WF-0915-1202. It selected “General question” and asked whether the separate freight charge could be split between two departments. It did not ask for a refund, repayment, credit, or cancellation. The entry used the same booking reference, so it appears in the same case search results. Its inclusion in the search results does not make it part of the refund request. The reviewer tagged it “billing inquiry.”

A second later entry appears on 17 September at 08:26, receipt number WF-0917-0826. It selected “Amendment” and asked to change the collection window from 13 October morning to 13 October afternoon, if available. The entry was recorded as submitted and contained the booking reference. The comment explicitly stated that the customer was requesting a schedule change, not a refund. The form system routed it to the operations team. It did not replace the earlier refund entry and did not change the date associated with the refund request.

Section 5. Date ledger and system verification
The finance system’s settled-payment field is 25 August 2026. The issued invoice date is 21 August 2026. The form receipt relevant to the refund is 4 September 2026. The event date is 12 October 2026. The case review dates, including 8 September, 11 September, and 13 September, are later administrative actions. Under Clause 4.2, the thirty-day deadline is calculated from 25 August, with 25 August as day zero. Adding 30 calendar days gives 24 September 2026 as the last permissible receipt date. The 4 September receipt precedes that date. This ledger is included as a verification aid; the clauses and original records are controlling.

For the amendment period, the same payment date is day zero. Adding 10 calendar days to 25 August gives 4 September 2026 as the final permissible date for an amendment request. The amendment entry described in Section 4 was received on 17 September 2026. It falls after the calculated end date. The fact that the entry concerned a future collection window, and that the event itself was still weeks away, does not alter the contractual start date or the length of the submission period. The September 17 entry is a submitted amendment request but was received after the stated ten-calendar-day deadline.

The account clerk checked the arithmetic against a calendar tool on 16 September. The clerk counted 26 August as day one for both periods. The thirtieth day after 25 August is 24 September: 26–31 August account for six days; 1–24 September account for the remaining twenty-four days. The tenth day after 25 August is 4 September: 26–31 August account for six days; 1–4 September account for four days. The terms explicitly use calendar days and do not adjust a weekend date. Neither calculated deadline falls on a weekend in this instance, but the no-adjustment rule remains part of the governing text.

The ledger also includes non-controlling dates to prevent confusion. The estimate was issued 12 August. The invoice preview was saved 19 August. The final invoice was issued 21 August. Payment settled 25 August. The first refund-form draft was saved 3 September. The refund form was submitted 4 September. The account desk opened the queue 8 September. The customer asked about routing 9 September. The billing inquiry was received 15 September. The schedule amendment was submitted 17 September. The packet was compiled 18 September. The event was planned for 12 October. Each entry has a distinct administrative meaning.

Section 6. Delivery and room-planning record
Foxglove Freight’s dispatch sheet lists a proposed delivery slot for 11 October 2026, 15:00–17:00. The site contact confirmed access for that slot on 6 October. The freight carrier’s proof-of-delivery scan records arrival at the service entrance at 15:42 on 11 October. The venue receiving clerk signed at 15:51. The event furniture was brought into the assigned holding area, and the equipment inventory was reconciled against the invoice. The delivery record is included to document performance and does not serve as the start date for either request period.

The collection plan lists 13 October 2026. The original window was 08:00–11:00. The later form entry requested an afternoon window, subject to availability. The dispatch desk’s note dated 18 September says the requested time had not yet been accepted. An operationally pending request remains distinct from a confirmed schedule change. The collection record was not yet signed when this consolidated packet was produced. Staff reserved the original window pending review of the later request.

The room-planning team maintained several versions of the floor plan. Version 1 was circulated on 18 August, before the invoice was issued. Version 2 was circulated on 20 August, after the invoice preview. Version 3 was circulated on 25 August, the day payment settled. Version 4, marked “working copy,” was circulated on 2 September. Version 5, marked “final layout for reception,” was attached to the 4 September refund form. The plans contain alternate table placements but do not alter the number of tables invoiced. The customer’s comment on the submitted form expressly sought repayment for the table charge, not merely approval of a new floor plan.

The seating plan notes 96 chairs in the plenary, 24 stools in the gallery, and a maximum planned occupancy of 132 people across the listed areas. A room-capacity check on 22 August found that circulation space was sufficient. A later attendance estimate on 28 August listed 118 expected participants. The attendance estimate is not a payment record, and it does not change the terms’ deadline. The catering worksheet has 120 meal portions, while the registration export has 117 confirmed responses and 9 pending responses. These counts are retained for operational planning and are not evidence that any invoice amount was paid or refunded.

A floor manager’s worksheet contains the note “two tables may be unnecessary if reception remains in Gallery.” The word “may” reflected a layout option under consideration. The customer did not use the worksheet itself to submit the refund request. The final form entry separately selected a refund request and identified the eight-table invoice line. That distinction is recorded because planning documents can be revised without transmitting a formal request under the terms.

The setup team’s room-by-room checklist lists the plenary, Workshop A, Workshop B, Workshop C, registration corridor, sponsor display area, and North Gallery. It gives each space a responsible lead and a key-access time. Workshop A was assigned to the east room, Workshop B to the west room, and Workshop C to the small annex. The original plan allocated six tables to each workshop room. The updated working plan moved two tables from the reception area to the sponsor display area but did not create a new purchase order. The checklist was last reviewed on 14 September and bears the approval initials of the facilities coordinator.

The accessibility review was completed on 7 September. It checked aisle width, lift access, reserved seating, and the path between the reception area and the accessible washroom. The review records no blocking issue. The reviewer asked that the final layout preserve a 1.2-meter route near the gallery entrance. The floor manager acknowledged the recommendation on 8 September. This operational exchange is not related to the date arithmetic for refund or amendment requests, but it explains why the layout documents were retained alongside the request record.

Section 7. Internal account-handling procedure
The account desk uses a four-stage workflow: intake, classification, review, and closure. Intake captures the original system timestamp and assigns a receipt number. Classification identifies whether an entry is a refund request, an amendment, a general billing inquiry, or an operational message. Review compares the submission with the terms, invoice, payment record, and supporting material. Closure records the decision or the reason a decision remains pending. Staff are expected to preserve the original record and not overwrite a timestamp during later processing.

At intake, the assigned clerk checks whether the form contains a customer identity and booking reference. If either is missing, the clerk flags the record for clarification. A clarification message is kept with the original form. The clerk does not treat the day of clarification as the receipt date when the initial entry already identifies the relevant booking and action. Where a customer submits multiple forms, each receives its own number, even when staff later attach them to a shared case file. This allows the reviewer to distinguish a request from a later inquiry or amendment.

During classification, the clerk reads the selected request type and the customer’s comment. The selected category is useful but not conclusive when the comment clearly describes a different administrative action. In this file, the 4 September entry’s type and comment both indicate a refund request. The 15 September entry is an inquiry about allocating the freight charge internally. The 17 September entry asks for a collection-window change. The system groups all three under the booking because they share a reference, but the customer’s requested action differs in each record.

The review stage records the applicable contractual period, the event that starts it, the number of days, and the system receipt date. Reviewers are instructed to write the computation rather than merely enter “in time” or “late.” For a 30-calendar-day period after a payment date of 25 August, the last day is 24 September. For a 10-calendar-day period after that same payment date, the last day is 4 September. A request date is compared with the proper period for that specific request type. The reviewer does not use the event date just because the event is prominent in the booking file.

The workflow separates timeliness from eligibility on the merits. A timely request is not automatically granted. The reviewer may still assess whether the requested amount corresponds to a billed item, whether the contract permits repayment, and whether the relevant service was provided. A late request is still recorded and reviewed according to internal procedure, but the system does not label it timely merely because it was received before the event. This packet asks only about the submission dates and requested actions; it does not make a final decision about the amount to be paid back.

The account desk is expected to send an acknowledgement within three business days where staffing permits. This is a service target, not a revised submission deadline. A message acknowledging receipt may be sent after the customer’s form has been in the queue for several days. The acknowledgement date should not replace the recorded receipt date. The same rule applies when an employee opens a form after a weekend, a leave day, or a period of high volume. The customer-facing receipt remains based on the stored submission timestamp.

If a duplicate or correction appears, the reviewer compares the substantive content. A repeated copy of an already complete request remains associated with the earlier request. A new requested action is logged as a new request. A request for a different delivery or collection time is treated as an amendment, even where it appears in the same case as a refund matter. A question about where to send a bill is a billing inquiry. Staff should not infer a refund request solely from the appearance of an invoice amount in a form comment.

Section 8. Correspondence register
On 21 August 2026, Granite Rentals emailed the final invoice to Harbor Labs. The message instructed the customer to retain the invoice number for all follow-up. The invoice email noted the scheduled event date and directed the customer to the service terms for deadlines. The email was sent at 11:34 local time. The message was delivered successfully; no delivery failure or resending record appears in the account history.

On 24 August, Harbor Labs’ finance unit created a payment instruction. The instruction named the correct invoice and amount. The bank file shows that the payment instruction was released on 25 August, and Granite Rentals’ system marked it settled on the same date. The internal finance worksheet bears a 24 August preparation date. Staff have not used that worksheet date as the settlement date because the vendor’s transaction record reports settlement on 25 August.

On 26 August, the finance clerk emailed Granite Rentals asking for a paid-balance confirmation. The clerk’s message included the invoice number and the customer’s purchase-order reference. Granite Rentals replied on 27 August with a statement showing a zero balance. The reply did not state that Harbor Labs had surrendered rights to make a request under the terms. The statement date was 27 August and is not a substitute for the settlement date in Clause 4.2.

On 28 August, the event coordinator sent the supplier a revised room plan. The email asked whether the vendor could accommodate a possible repositioning of display panels. It did not ask for a refund, and it did not submit a change to the number of reception tables. Granite Rentals replied that the layout could be reviewed at the site meeting. The exchange was filed under planning correspondence.

On 2 September, Harbor Labs’ event team circulated an internal note stating that the final guest plan was being reconciled. The note mentioned that eight reception tables were still on the invoice. It did not instruct Granite Rentals to refund or remove them. The account desk was not included on the internal circulation list. A copy was later included as background with the 4 September web-form entry, but the form’s server timestamp remains the time the refund request was received.

On 4 September, the web-form system recorded the refund request. The receipt page displayed the booking reference, request type, amount, and submission time. The form exporter identifies the request as submitted, and the receipt email reached the customer mailbox at 16:42. The one-minute difference reflects the outbound email process; it does not change the form receipt time. The account desk’s case screen retained the 16:41 timestamp.

On 8 September, a staff member opened the form and assigned it to the account review queue. The staff member’s note says, “Customer requests return of reception table charge; check terms and service status.” The note correctly summarizes the form. The date on the staff note is not the customer submission date. On 10 September, the desk acknowledged receipt and advised that the review remained underway. The acknowledgement did not alter the receipt record.

On 15 September, Harbor Labs asked whether the delivery-and-collection charge could be allocated between its finance cost centers. The email link opened the general-question form, and the system recorded a billing inquiry. The message does not ask Granite Rentals to return that charge. The inquiry is included because it shares the invoice reference and appears near the other entries in the case export.

On 17 September, the event coordinator submitted a request to change the collection time. The request was entered using the amendment form and was assigned a new receipt number. The customer stated that the event schedule had shifted and asked whether collection could occur in the afternoon rather than the morning. Granite Rentals had not accepted or rejected that requested schedule at the time the packet was compiled. The entry is a request for an amendment, and its receipt date is the date stored by the platform.

Section 9. Records-management appendix
The event file is maintained in the customer-services archive under reference HL-2048. The archive administrator preserves source records in their original formats where possible. PDF copies are generated for the review packet, but generated-copy dates are not treated as dates of the events shown in those documents. The archive lists a creation date, a last-modified date, and an underlying transaction date where available. Staff should use the underlying date appropriate to the clause being applied.

The invoice PDF was generated again on 18 September for inclusion in this packet. Its original issue date remains 21 August. The payment confirmation was downloaded on 26 August, one day after settlement. The form receipt was downloaded on 4 September. The account case export was generated on 18 September and therefore shows later notes as well as the original form record. These file-generation dates support document custody but do not change the content of the original transaction or submission.

The archive’s indexed document list includes: GR-66108 invoice; HL-PO-778 purchase order; bank settlement confirmation; WF-0904-1641 refund-form receipt; reception layout attachment; account acknowledgement; 15 September billing inquiry; WF-0917-0826 amendment receipt; dispatch sheet; site access confirmation; delivery scan; and collection planning note. The index is an inventory. A document’s presence in the archive is not, on its own, evidence that a refund has been approved or that a requested schedule change has been implemented.

The archive administrator performed a duplicate check on 18 September. The administrator found no second submitted refund form before the 4 September receipt. The 3 September entry was classified as an abandoned draft and did not have a submission timestamp. The administrator found no corrected refund request that replaced the original. The later billing inquiry and amendment request were retained as separate entries because their selected actions differed from the refund form.

The handling guide requires the account desk to preserve both the original form fields and any later correspondence. If a user calls instead of submitting a form, the employee may record the call, but the terms still require the request to reach the designated form. The call record cannot be substituted for a form submission unless an authorized exception is documented. No such exception appears in this file. The customer’s relevant refund action is supported by the actual submitted web form, rather than by a call or a staff-created note.

A correction to a transcription error in the packet should be made in a dated addendum rather than by editing the source invoice or form receipt. The addendum must identify the record corrected, the reason, and the author. No addendum altering the payment date, invoice date, form receipt date, or event date is present. The dates reproduced in this packet therefore remain consistent with the vendor system and customer submission records.

Section 10. Operational checklist and status table
Checklist item A: Invoice issued. Status: complete. Record: GR-66108, issued 21 August 2026. The invoice names Harbor Labs, the event, and the service lines. The purchase-order match was verified. The invoice status is not a request status.

Checklist item B: Payment settled. Status: complete. Record: settled 25 August 2026. Amount: $8,460.00. The finance account reflects no outstanding balance. The settlement date is the triggering date for the periods in Clauses 4.2 and 4.5.

Checklist item C: Refund submission received. Status: complete. Record: WF-0904-1641. Receipt: 4 September 2026 at 16:41. Request type: refund. Requested item: reception-table line. Requested amount: $560.00. The submission is distinct from its review and acknowledgement dates.

Checklist item D: Refund review complete. Status: pending at compilation. The reviewer has confirmed receipt and is checking the terms and service record. A pending merits review does not prevent determination of the submission date. This packet does not state that a payment has been returned.

Checklist item E: General billing inquiry. Status: received 15 September 2026. Subject: internal allocation of the delivery-and-collection charge. Requested action: information about cost-center allocation. No refund request is recorded in that entry.

Checklist item F: Collection amendment. Status: received 17 September 2026. Requested action: move collection from the morning to the afternoon on 13 October. Review status: pending. The submitted action is an amendment request; the operations team had not yet confirmed the requested window when this packet was compiled.

Checklist item G: Delivery performance. Status: delivery scan recorded 11 October in the dispatch plan; final proof-of-delivery record to be filed after the event. The planning schedule includes the scan and receiving details described above. This item is maintained separately from the refund and amendment deadlines.

Checklist item H: Event closeout. Status: not yet due at packet compilation. The event is scheduled for 12 October 2026. Closeout will include a returned-equipment count, signed collection record, and any approved account adjustment. The closeout date does not change the payment-relative deadlines already stated.

Section 11. Staff guidance concerning date fields
The customer portal displays several dates in different places. “Invoice date” identifies when the invoice was issued. “Payment date” identifies when funds settled. “Submitted on” identifies when the customer completed the form transmission. “Reviewed on” identifies when staff first opened or processed the record. “Event date” identifies when services are scheduled. A screen may show more than one of these fields together, and staff are expected to select the field named by the relevant clause rather than the most recent or visually prominent date.

A date typed into a comment is not necessarily the submission date. A date printed on an attachment is not necessarily the submission date. A message sent after a form may confirm or discuss the request without changing the form’s original timestamp. Conversely, a pre-submission draft may contain text describing an intended request without constituting a received request. The system’s receipt event is the controlling record for a form submission under the attached terms.

When calculating a calendar-day period, the reviewer starts with the day after the triggering date as day one. For this file, the payment settled on 25 August. Thus, 26 August is day one, 31 August is day six, and 1 September is day seven. This sequence continues without interruption through weekends. Day ten is 4 September, and day thirty is 24 September. No rule in the attached terms pauses the count for review, internal routing, or the event’s proximity.

The clerk should also distinguish an event’s requested date from the date the request is made. The collection amendment concerns a service date of 13 October, but it was submitted on 17 September. A customer may request a future change well before the service date and still be outside a payment-relative submission period. The fact that a request concerns an event that has not yet occurred does not by itself make the request timely under a clause measured from payment.

If a request asks for more than one type of action, staff should identify each action separately. A request for an item refund can be assessed under Clause 4.2. A requested change in collection timing is assessed under Clause 4.5. A question about cost allocation is processed as a billing inquiry. Similar wording about invoice charges does not erase the distinctions among these administrative categories.

Section 12. Supporting statements from the event team
The event coordinator’s planning statement, dated 16 September, says that the reception layout had changed several times during planning. The statement explains that the team explored using fewer tables, moving tables into the gallery, and holding a standing reception. It records that the final decision about requesting a refund was entered into the web form on 4 September. The statement is supplemental context and is consistent with the form receipt. It does not claim that the customer made the request on the date of an earlier internal layout discussion.

The finance liaison’s statement, dated 17 September, confirms that the payment was settled through the vendor account on 25 August. The liaison notes that the purchase order was approved on 24 August and that an internal payment instruction was prepared that day. The liaison distinguishes preparation and approval from settlement. The vendor transaction record and the finance statement agree on the settled date.

The facilities lead’s statement, dated 17 September, confirms that the collection time request concerns operational convenience after the program schedule was revised. The facilities lead says the afternoon window would be preferable but acknowledges that Granite Rentals had not accepted the change. The statement does not identify a different receipt date for the request and does not claim that the request was made within the ten-day period.

The account reviewer’s work note, dated 18 September, says the file should be evaluated against the exact clauses and timestamps, without treating internal discussions as formal submissions. The reviewer lists three forms: a refund submission on 4 September, an inquiry on 15 September, and an amendment submission on 17 September. The reviewer’s note does not decide whether the refund should be granted on its merits or whether the supplier can operationally accommodate the requested collection time.

Section 13. Audit observations and reconciliation notes
An audit sample was performed to confirm the relationship between the invoice total and the payment record. The auditor added the line amounts shown on GR-66108 and compared the result with the settled amount. The account system shows the invoice paid in full. No partial payment, reversed payment, chargeback, or second payment is listed. These details are included to establish the payment event for the deadline calculations, not to determine the refund’s merits.

The auditor also compared the three relevant web-form entries. The first is a submitted refund request with a receipt timestamp. The second is a general billing inquiry. The third is an amendment request with a separate receipt timestamp. The auditor verified that each entry carries the same booking reference but has a different request type. The common reference makes the entries searchable together; it does not make them one submission with one date.

The audit report notes that the date the account desk opened the refund record is later than the system receipt date. The auditor treated the stored form timestamp as the submission date, in accordance with Clause 4.2. The report also notes that the future collection date is later than the amendment submission date, but that the amendment clause measures from payment rather than from the requested collection date. The report therefore records the applicable trigger and the calculated final date for each period.

No separate term in the packet grants an extension because a request concerns a future service date, because a customer’s internal team needed time to approve a layout, or because the supplier’s staff reviewed a form after receipt. The terms contain a specific weekend rule, but the calculated final dates here are ordinary calendar dates. The audit did not identify an approved exception to the stated periods.

The file’s reconciliation table has a status column for each record. Invoice: issued. Payment: settled. Refund form: submitted, timely under the 30-day calculation, merits review pending. Billing inquiry: submitted as a general question, no refund action stated. Amendment form: submitted, outside the 10-day period, operational review pending. Delivery: recorded in the logistics section. Collection: planned, with a requested change awaiting review. The table records the audit’s classification and does not approve or deny any monetary adjustment.

Section 14. Retention of ancillary planning material
The packet includes ancillary material because the file was assembled from several operational folders. The venue access map was revised twice to show the service entrance. The first map was circulated on 11 August and the second on 23 August. The map revision log records that the freight driver should use the east loading bay. It does not include a payment instruction, a refund request, or an amendment submission.

A draft program lists the plenary at 09:00, workshops from 10:30, lunch at 12:15, and the reception at 17:30. A later program moves the reception opening to 18:00. The program version history includes edits on 27 August and 6 September. These program times are event-planning details. They do not modify the dates of payment or receipt in the vendor account.

The registration team’s materials include a badge-printing schedule, dietary-preference spreadsheet, and volunteer roster. The badge-printing schedule was prepared on 5 September. The dietary spreadsheet was updated on 9 September, and the roster was reviewed on 12 September. The files are held in the event folder but do not relate to the form submissions being reviewed. The archive avoids deleting such material because it may be needed for post-event reconciliation.

A supplier contact sheet lists the account desk, dispatch queue, venue supervisor, and event coordinator. The sheet was created on 18 August and updated on 8 September. It identifies which channel to use for an account request and which channel to use for operational questions. The web-form terms require the designated form for formal submissions. Email and telephone contacts may be used for follow-up, but the contact sheet does not change the submission requirements.

The equipment inventory includes serial labels for the modular riser and folding display panels, and a count sheet for the chairs, tables, stools, and microphone sets. The inventory is intended for delivery and return checks. A pre-event inspection is scheduled for 11 October. The final inventory may be signed after the event and filed during closeout. Neither the inspection nor the closeout schedule adjusts the request periods measured from the 25 August settlement.

A venue safety note dated 30 August identifies a temporary barrier near the gallery entrance and asks that the route remain unobstructed. The operations team acknowledged the note on 31 August. The barrier was removed on 1 September. The safety note contains dates close to the form draft and submission dates, but it is not an account request. It has no effect on the receipt timestamps or on the term’s day-counting method.

The event coordinator’s working calendar contains reminders for the invoice review, the form follow-up, the site meeting, and the event closeout. A reminder entered on a calendar may be generated before or after the relevant action. Calendar reminders are not treated as proof that a customer transmitted a form. The original system record remains available for each action at issue.

Section 15. Final filing statement
This consolidated packet was assembled on 18 September 2026 by the Harbor Labs event administration unit. The assembler compared the invoice, settlement record, service terms, web-form export, and account notes. The assembler did not revise source timestamps and did not make a determination about the ultimate refund entitlement or the operational feasibility of the collection-time change. The materials are filed to support a consistent review of request type and deadline status.

The controlling record for payment is Granite Rentals’ settled-payment entry dated 25 August 2026. The controlling record for the refund request is the submitted web form WF-0904-1641, received 4 September 2026. The controlling record for the collection-window amendment is WF-0917-0826, received 17 September 2026. The terms measure the refund period as 30 calendar days after settlement and the amendment period as 10 calendar days after settlement. Day zero is the settlement date. The resulting last dates are 24 September and 4 September, respectively.

The file therefore preserves a timely submitted refund request for the reception-table charge and a later submitted request to amend the collection window. The former is within its applicable 30-calendar-day submission period. The latter is beyond its applicable 10-calendar-day submission period. The general billing inquiry does not request a refund. These classifications describe the records and time limits only; they do not state that a refund has been approved, that the requested schedule change has been granted, or that any additional service has been ordered.

End of consolidated file. The invoice, terms excerpt, web-form entries, logistics notes, and correspondence register remain separately searchable under HL-2048. All date computations in this packet use the vendor’s settled-payment date and the counting convention printed in the terms.
